items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2001 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Even today, there’s about four guys, five guys, that are still left from the original. Because most of them are dead. A lot of them are dead unfortunately, Richie Kamuca is dead, Mel Lewis is dead, Buddy Clarke is dead, Joe Maini is dead, Ray Cheschare, Frank Rosolino.

ctx.x: And colleges are buying them left and right. I was just doing a clinic and a few of the college people said, “Are you kidding, we ordered fourteen.” Because they don’t write arrangements like that anymore. They’re just straight ahead swing music. And especially if you want to show the band off, if you play the arrangements like it’s really written, because I actually patterned the band after the Benny Goodman band because Benny played in and out. Because it didn’t blend with the section. It did, but it would…

better, he still forgot to turn the page over, so he came in again, and I have to play after that, the vibes play. Then comes the clarinet. So he’s picking up the clarinet and he’s playing all alone while I’m playing my solo. Then he realizes what he’s doing. Once again the audience fell out, and you know what? That was the standard thing through the whole hour and a half we do. I’d asked Med, “Med, you want to sing?” “Anything you want, Terry.” And Med’s very funny. All the guys. items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: what he said when it was his birthday with the Dream Band played “Happy Birthday” to him

ctx.x: Um hum. If I put Terry Gibbs and Jack Sheldon and Chubby Jackson in a room together, I wonder what might occur?

Well first you’d have to call the insane asylum. You call the insane asylum and make a reservation at the insane asylum. Because I don’t know it would be a lot of laughs. Talk about — Chubby and I had — a completely differently than Jack and I did. I’ll tell you about Jack. You know Jack could get a little risqué on stage. But when he worked with me he knew that he could not do that. I’m selling music and I’ll be the straight man, and Jack is funny without having to be dirty. You know he’s funny. He’s got a great…

Yes. So we’ve been at this for about an hour, I’ve really enjoyed this. I want to wrap up with a couple of questions. I wonder if you could have done anything else in your life besides being a musician.
